name: MutableString concurrent publication preserves complete Unicode

input.source_text: module M { public fun run() -> String { let text = m"old"; concurrently_replace(text, "new"); text.to_string() } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Requires concurrent execution, and the blocker is structural rather than a missing API. MutableString itself exists: `m"old"` builds one, `replace` mutates it and `to_string` reads it back. What is absent is any way for a SECOND thread to hold an Iris value at all: runtime values are `Rc<RefCell<..>>` - MutableStringRef, ArrayRef, HashRef and ByteArrayRef all are - so they are not `Send` and cannot cross a thread boundary even from Rust. C060's observable is what a correctly synchronized observer sees DURING an unsynchronized write, so it cannot be reached until runtime values are shareable. Real threads do exist in the ABI layer's own tests, but they carry copied integers across the C boundary and never touch an Iris value, which is exactly what FFI-C013 requires of them.

expect.status: A correctly synchronized observer receives either old complete content or new complete content and never invalid Unicode.
